draft.title: The cardiovascular system
card: The heart is a muscular pump. It pushes blood around the body in a loop of blood vessels.
carry blood away from the heart. Their walls are thick and strong to handle the pressure of each heartbeat.
are tiny vessels with very thin walls. Oxygen and nutrients pass out to the muscles here, and waste such as carbon dioxide passes in.
carry blood back to the heart. Blood in them is under lower pressure than in arteries.
draft.remember: The heart pumps blood out in arteries, through capillaries to swap with muscles, and back in veins.

a.q: Which vessels let oxygen pass out to the muscles and waste pass in?
a.why: Capillary walls are very thin, so oxygen and nutrients can pass out to the muscles while waste passes in. Arteries are tempting because they carry blood away from the heart, but their thick walls are built for pressure, not for exchange.
a.clue: Look for the vessels with very thin walls.

b.q: Jai is running. Blood leaves his heart and travels to his thigh muscles. Which vessels carry it away from the heart?
b.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, so they take blood towards the thigh muscles. Veins are tempting because they are large vessels, but they carry blood back to the heart.
b.clue: Think about the direction the blood is moving.
